title: WordPress Database Connection Error
demandEvidence: Research-backed editorial queue topic from official WordPress troubleshooting documentation. Search demand, impressions, and community volume have not been measured for this brief.
whyWeCanWin: Focus the guide on distinguishing configuration issues from host/database availability problems, preserving sensitive credentials, and knowing when to contact the host. This narrower troubleshooting intent complements the existing general site-down and plugin-conflict checklists.
outline: What the database-connection error indicates and what it does not diagnose by itself
Record the exact message, affected URLs, recent changes, and provider alerts before changing files
Check whether the host reports a database or resource issue before editing configuration
Protect credentials and backups; avoid publishing or copying wp-config.php contents
When to involve the hosting provider or a WordPress technician

review.feedback: The draft offers credible, evidence-led troubleshooting guidance with strong internal linking and authoritative citations. It passes the numerical threshold, but the missing FAQ blocks compliance with the required delivery format. A concrete diagnostic example and tighter handling of repeated cautions would improve usefulness.
suggestions: End with an FAQ containing 3–5 questions covering data loss, intermittent failures, database credentials, hosting support, and when a restore is appropriate.
Add a clearly labeled hypothetical migration example showing how a technician distinguishes an incorrect DB_HOST value from an unavailable database service.
Consolidate repeated security and backup cautions to make room for the FAQ while keeping the final article within 1,800–2,200 words.
Verify all four internal destinations and confirm the final word count before publication.
